candidates.summary: The `$` exception in titleEscapeSet rests on a false premise: gnoweb unescapes `\$` in a link title, so the exception changes nothing visible and keeps the one escape set where `$` still opens math
candidates.failure_scenario: The code comment (markdown.go:89-91), the ADR's Decision and the PR body say gnoweb shows a title's backslashes, so "Price $5" would read "Price \$5". Run at 82a20872a: `[a](/r/x "Price $5 v1\.0 \$6")` renders title="Price $5 v1.0 $6", and a reference definition `[l]: /r/x "Price $x^{2}$ v1\.0"` renders title="Price $x^{2}$ v1.0". Escaping `$` in a title costs nothing, the same as `\.` already costs nothing. Keeping it out has a latent cost: title-shaped text that does not parse as a link, `[a]( "Price $x^{2}$")`, renders x^{2} as math, while `[a]( "Price \$x^{2}\$")` stays text. Today no reader loses anything: LinkTitle's only caller, LinkReferenceDefinition, always emits a definition that parses. Fix: drop lines 89-92 and TestEscapeTitle's "Price $5" case, so the title set is the inline set plus the two quotes.

candidates.failure_scenario: The fix rests on the claim that `\$` renders as a plain dollar and never opens math. That holds today in a paragraph, a link label, an image alt, a strong span, an alert title, a GFM cell, a heading, the TOC and the Lead title (run). But TestEscapeInline only asserts `\$x\$`.
